hints: Focus on the type of reaction here, ethanal with HCN is nucleophilic addition to form a cyanohydrin.
Write out the reactants, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ and $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N}$, and the product, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$, then compare which atoms join together.
Check each bond carefully, which new C-C link appears, which H-C link in HCN must split, and does the very strong $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond ever break?
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction**

This is nucleophilic addition of HCN to an aldehyde to make a hydroxynitrile (cyanohydrin). Think of $\text{CN}^-$ attacking the carbonyl carbon, then protonation of the oxygen.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Check statement 1, C-C bond formed**

The carbonyl carbon of ethanal joins to the carbon of the cyanide group. That creates a brand new carbon-carbon single bond in the product. So statement 1 is true.

**Check statements 2 and 3, bonds broken**

In $\text{H-C}\equiv\text{N}$, the $\text{H-C}$ bond must break to supply $\text{CN}^-$ (nucleophile) and later $\text{H}^+$ (to protonate the $\text{O}^-$). That is a carbon-hydrogen bond broken, so statement 2 is true.

The $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond stays intact all the way through and appears unchanged in the product. No carbon-nitrogen bond is broken, so statement 3 is false.

**Combine the conclusion**

Only 1 and 2 are correct. That combination corresponds to option B.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. While 1 and 2 are true, 3 is false because the $\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ bond in cyanide is not broken, it is carried straight into the cyanohydrin product.
options.B: Correct. A new C-C bond forms between the aldehyde carbon and the CN carbon (1 is true), and the H-C bond of HCN breaks to give $\text{CN}^-$ and $\text{H}^+$ (2 is true), while the C-N bond remains intact (3 is false).
options.C: Incorrect. This would require 2 and 3 only, missing 1. Statement 1 is definitely true because nucleophilic addition of $\text{CN}^-$ to $\text{C=O}$ always creates a new C-C bond, and statement 3 is false.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean only 1 is correct. Statement 2 is also correct because HCN must lose H from carbon to act as $\text{CN}^-$ nucleophile, so H-C bond breaking does occur.
